_: The claims this rung makes, and how many assertions each one is.
Two readers, and they are the reason this file exists rather than a number in a sentence.
When the rung RUNS, crates/daemon/tests/web_browser.rs compares this list against
Playwright's own JSON report — every title, in order, and every title's count of
`expect` steps — so a claim added to a spec and not to this file is red, and so is a
claim that quietly stopped asserting half of what it used to. When the rung SKIPS, this
is where the skip line gets the number it reports: `N claims, M assertions, not run`.
A skip that cannot say what it did not do is the skip that reads as a pass.
The counts are measured, never estimated: they come out of a green run's report, and
the harness names this file in its failure message when they drift.

claims.title: a sparse menu becomes a select carrying the device's own indices
claims.what: PF:2 — the device's own menu indices reach a <select>, holes and all

claims.title: an INACTIVE control is still usable and names what owns it
claims.what: PF:3 — an INACTIVE control renders enabled, badged and named, beside a READ_ONLY one that does not [PF:12]

claims.title: a current outside its declared range renders with no min and no max
claims.what: PF:4 — an out-of-range current is shown, and no attribute bounds it

claims.title: a control type this build cannot name shows its raw discriminant
claims.what: PF:1 — an unnameable control type renders its discriminant and payload

claims.title: a clamp snaps the slider back and says both numbers
claims.what: PF:6/D3 — a clamped write moves the slider back and shows both numbers

claims.title: a menu whose value the device did not report selects nothing
claims.what: a control with no current renders a selected, disabled placeholder rather than the browser's first option

claims.title: a scalar whose value the device did not report draws no slider
claims.what: N199 — a range input has to hold a number, so a control with no current gets none: no slider, an empty field, and nothing written by a gesture

claims.title: the bitmask field refuses what it cannot write, and says when a write is in flight
claims.what: an emptied or unparsable bitmask writes nothing and says so, and an in-flight write is painted rather than only recorded

claims.title: the preview paints successive frames and keeps painting across a photo
claims.what: the MJPEG paints successive parts, keeps painting across a photo (N83), and the photo's report names its formats as MJPG-style fourccs rather than as four numbers (N109)

claims.title: the preview paints a recording's own frames and the page says who owns the camera
claims.what: N117 — the ruling from a viewer's side: the keeps painting a recording's own frames on the request it already had, and #recording-status says who owns the camera and for how long

claims.title: the calibration view tracks a sweep it did not start
claims.what: the calibration view paints a sweep started on another socket

claims.title: the client loads with no credential and the camera is still refused
claims.what: N82 — the module graph loads and runs anonymously, the two camera routes do not, and the page names the two candidates a page with no token actually has

claims.title: a page in another origin cannot reach the camera, token and all
claims.what: N93 — a sandboxed iframe's and WebSocket are refused 403 by the daemon, with this run's token in both URLs

claims.title: the page reports a lost socket and works again on the next one
claims.what: the socket's loss is reported, the preview is ended, and the next socket works

claims.title: a socket that closed refuses the next call instead of parking it
claims.what: a call made after the close is refused at once — WHATWG's silent `send()` on a CLOSED socket would otherwise park it for ever — and the click that used to undo the close is answered

claims.title: a subscription that died with the socket stops saying it is watching
claims.what: E16 §1's class again: every stream is told the socket ended, and no writer of #connection contradicts the one sentence that covers it

claims.title: a preview the page walked away from is a preview the daemon stopped
claims.what: docs/11 H4 — a camera the page stops previewing is a camera the daemon stops streaming, read through the viewer cap that is the only count a browser can see

claims.title: the control panel on screen belongs to the camera on screen
claims.what: docs/11 M32 — the panel is emptied in the same task as the click, and an answer about a camera the page has walked away from is dropped rather than painted

claims.title: a refused camera list at startup is a sentence rather than a silence
claims.what: docs/11 M33 — a refused wch_list at startup reaches the banner instead of becoming an unhandled rejection under the word `connected`

claims.title: a recording answer in flight is not written under the next camera's picture
claims.what: docs/11 L36 — an answer that arrives after the handle was retired writes nothing into #recording-status

claims.title: a socket severed without a FIN stops reading as connected
claims.what: docs/11 L38 — the idle heartbeat ends a connection that stopped carrying anything without ever closing, on a clock the test owns

claims.title: an idle socket is kept by an answer, and a slow call is not a dead socket
claims.what: L38's healthy path: the heartbeat is answered over the route the page opens (A9 — the dependency claim the rung had never run), a call that merely timed out is refused as a timeout and leaves the connection alone, and silence still ends it

claims.title: a stale session list is not painted under the camera on screen
claims.what: docs/11 M32's third element — a wch_calibrate_list answer about a camera the page has walked away from paints nothing, in the success arm and the refusal arm

claims.title: the browser this rung drove is the pinned one
claims.what: the Playwright package and the Chromium build that ran are the pinned ones

claims.title: the preview and the control being adjusted are visible together at every scroll position
claims.what: D20 — the workbench's layout requirement, at the rung's pinned viewport over the 77-control profile: the document does not scroll, the control column does, and the preview's box does not move at any scroll position of it

claims.title: a narrow viewport stacks the shell and keeps the preview at the top
claims.what: D20 — the same claim one column wide, both halves of it: the shell really stacks (one column, the panes one above the other, the document the scroll container), and the preview is stuck to its top rather than merely somewhere on the screen — the half that was asserted before is true in either layout

claims.title: a session driven from the page records the operator's own choice
claims.what: D20 — the whole human-driven flow through the buttons an operator uses, Apply and Restore included, with `selector: human`, the goal and the criteria the operator typed asserted on a second socket rather than through the page's own belief; the sample photographs really decode through /session-photo and stop decoding without the token; the page stands its own preview down before the sweep, which is N83's boundary and E16's collision answered

claims.title: the sweep-time pane becomes the sweep and paints each sample as its event lands
claims.what: D20's sweep-time pane swap, split off from the flow at P9c and landed now: the preview pane is handed to the sweep and handed back, the progress line advances on `wch_subscribe_calibration`'s own index/total, and each sample is painted through /session-photo as its event arrives

claims.title: a sweep the device refused hands the pane back with the device's own reason painted in it
claims.what: D20's "handed back on every ending a sweep has, refusals included", for the sentence and not only the `hidden` bit: the fake refuses `auto_exposure`'s first write, and the pane reads out `sweep_interrupted`'s discriminant and message before the preview takes the slot back (N278)

claims.title: a stale session document is not painted over the sample the operator chose
claims.what: docs/11 M32's fourth element — a late `wch_calibrate_status` answer marks neither the wrong sample nor writes the wrong sentence, with the current answer asserted to have painted (N154, N156)

claims.title: an out-of-order click is the daemon's refusal, rendered, and the flow carries on
claims.what: D20 — the state machine's refusals are the page's guard rails rather than duplicated client-side logic: an illegal step is sent, refused, rendered with its D13 kind *and the whole of its instruction-last message*, and the next legal step works; the two halves of that message are asserted independently rather than one entailing the other (N250)

claims.title: a double-click on Sweep next is one sweep, and the page says so once
claims.what: N279 — the sweep is non-re-entrant at the door, so the gesture an operator makes without thinking starts one sweep: one `sweeping …` sentence, no `illegal_transition` on screen, and no refusal colour left over the success sentence

claims.title: a control refused because the camera was busy is offered again; one the daemon will not sweep is not
claims.what: AGENTS rule 7 at a button (N285) — `busy` is a fact about a machine at a moment and stays retryable, `illegal_transition` is a statement about the control and is remembered; the control each click chose is read off the page's own progress sentence

claims.title: a refused sweep leaves the samples the operator is reviewing on the screen
claims.what: N281 — `flow.reviewing` moves only when a sweep produced samples, so a refusal between a selection and the next verb does not empty the grid the human selector is judging in

claims.title: a session does not follow a camera, even when the start answer lands after the switch
claims.what: N280 — the M32 fence over the *assignment* and not only the read: a held `wch_calibrate_start` answer released after a camera switch is dropped rather than installed, so no verb afterwards is refused `fingerprint_mismatch`; the positive control is the same gesture with nothing to retire it

claims.title: a sweep in another session is a line in the log beside, never a picture in this pane
claims.what: N283 — the one-subscription fan-in's safety argument, driven: a real frame this daemon sent, replayed with its session rewritten, reaches the log below and not the operator's pane

claims.title: a refusal about a session nobody is looking at is not painted in red over a current line
claims.what: N283 — the louder half of M32's fourth element: a held `wch_calibrate_status` refusal released after a camera switch changes nothing on screen (N154, N156)
